# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🙏 👍 👎]

My thinking: I'm Deaf — the only one who can see the bomb, but I can't hear a word anyone says, so every reply I ever get must arrive as gestures. The action board shows a display reading **1**, a **green light**, and **seven wires** (1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue). That's everything visible; the rest is manual (Mute) and touch (Blind).

Channel map: my speech reaches both Mute and Blind, since both can hear. My gestures reach Mute only. Mute's only output is gestures to me; Blind's speech reaches Mute but never me — so Mute is the relay from Blind's hands to my eyes, and I am the bridge carrying Mute's manual knowledge to Blind, who would otherwise never receive any of it.

Mute opened with 👋 🙏 👍 👎. With no shared code yet, the natural read is: hello, please, yes, no — Mute is proposing a yes/no protocol. I'll confirm that read, formalize a code (thumbs up/down, folded hands for "question/need more", OK for "understood/go", repeated fist punches for numbers), and immediately put it to work with three ordered yes/no questions about the manual so next round I get real bits back: does the manual match this module, does the display number matter, does the light colour matter. Blind hears everything I say, so I define the same gesture code for Blind, tell Blind to report tactile findings by voice to Mute (who relays to me), and freeze all action until the manual rule is confirmed — one wrong move ends everything.

My calls:

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Both of you can hear me, but I cannot hear you at all, so answers must come to me only as hand gestures, which I can see. Everything I see on the bomb: a display showing the number 1. A light shining green. Seven wires in a row, numbered 1 to 7 from top to bottom: wire 1 red, wire 2 white, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 orange, wire 5 green, wire 6 purple, wire 7 blue. No labels, no buttons, nothing else printed anywhere. Mute, your four gestures reached me and I read them as hello, please, yes, no. If that is right, adopt this code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, folded hands means I have a question or I need more information, the OK sign means understood or go ahead, and a number is sent as that many fist punches, so three punches means 3. Answer next round with three signs in a row, one per question. Question 1: does the manual cover a bomb with a display, a light and seven wires? Question 2: do any instructions depend on the number shown on the display? Question 3: do any instructions depend on the colour of the light? Blind, you hear me and you can touch the bomb, but do not cut or press anything yet, one wrong action kills all three of us. Report to Mute by voice whatever you feel: batteries, buttons, labels, textures. You can also use the same gesture code toward me: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, fist punches for numbers. Mute, relay anything Blind tells you to me in our code. Nobody acts until the manual rule for this bomb is clear to me and confirmed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👋", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

My thinking: Reading this round's arrivals in order. Mute sent three thumbs up in a row — that is exactly the three-sign answer format I demanded, so: **yes** the manual covers a display/light/seven-wire bomb, **yes** the rules depend on the display number, **yes** they depend on the light colour. Then 👌 understood, then five punches — the number **5** — then 🙏 "question/need more info". Blind separately sent me 👌, confirming Blind heard my code and adopted it.

The most natural read of the 5 is: the manual's rule for display=1 + green light points at **wire 5** — the fifth from the top, the green one, which conveniently sits between orange (4) and purple (6) so Blind can find it blind by position. The trailing 🙏 tells me Mute may still need something, possibly facts only Blind's fingers can supply (batteries, a button, a serial). I can't ask Mute open questions — Mute answers only in our small code — so I extend the code with a few more signs (crossed fingers = "cut it, go"; raised hand = "stop"; pinch = "press a button"; pointing = count from top/bottom) and convert the ambiguity into three answerable yes/no questions. Timing note: I speak last in the round, so my words land on Mute and Blind at the start of the next round — meaning if Mute confirms with 👍 + crossed fingers, I can give Blind the go the round after, and Blind cuts having heard Mute's confirmation. Nobody acts until then.

My calls:

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. Received your three thumbs up: yes the manual covers this bomb, yes the rule depends on the display number, yes it depends on the light colour. Then OK, then five punches, then your question sign. I read the five as: the wire to cut is wire 5, the green one, fifth counting from the top. If that is wrong, answer thumbs down to my Question 1. New code additions, everyone use them from now on: crossed fingers means this is the wire to cut, go. Raised open hand means stop, hold, do not act. Pinch means press a button or switch. Finger pointing up means counting from the top, pointing down means counting from the bottom. Wire layout by position from the top: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. Answer me next round with signs in a row, in this order. Question 1: is the complete correct action right now to cut wire 5, the green wire, fifth from the top, and nothing else? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question 2: does the right choice depend on anything Blind can feel that I have not listed, such as batteries, a button or a serial number? Question 3: if you need more facts, send thumbs up followed by a number of punches for how many facts, and Blind and I will supply them. If Question 1 is yes, also end with crossed fingers, and that will be my authority to order the cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your OK reached me, good. Do not cut or press anything yet. Learn the wires by position, counting from the top: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. The likely target is wire 5, the green one: it is the fifth wire from the top, with orange as the fourth just above it and purple as the sixth just below it, so you can find it by feel without colour. While you wait, report to Mute by voice everything your hands find: how many batteries, any buttons or switches, any raised or printed serial characters and their shapes. Mute will relay it to me in our code. You will hear my explicit go before any wire is cut, and only on my say-so.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🤞]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

My thinking: The relay worked. Mute answered in exactly my three-sign format: 👍 yes — cutting wire 5 (green, fifth from top) and nothing else is the complete correct action; 👎 no — the rule does not depend on anything Blind can feel beyond what I already reported (consistent with Turn 2: the rule keys only off display and light colour, both of which I see and reported); and no punches followed, so no extra facts are wanted. Then 🤞 — crossed fingers — which per my own code is Mute's explicit "this is the wire to cut, go." Blind's second 👌 confirms Blind still has the code and is holding position. Every condition I set last round is now satisfied: manual-confirmed rule, matching bomb state, informed cutter. Waiting further only burns time on a live bomb, so this turn I give the execution order. I address it to Blind by voice with position-based identification (fifth from top, orange above, purple below) so colour-blindness of the scene doesn't matter, add an abort clause in case Blind's fingers find anything contradicting my layout, and demand a post-action sign so I can verify the outcome. A short acknowledgment and the 👍🤞👌 echo to Mute closes the loop on the relay.

My calls:

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the go. Mute has confirmed by our code that the complete and only correct action is to cut wire 5, the green wire. Identify it purely by position: it is the fifth wire counting from the top, with the orange wire as the fourth directly above it and the purple wire as the sixth directly below it. Cut that one wire only. Do not touch, pull or cut any other wire, do not press anything. Abort condition: if your fingers count a number of wires other than seven, or feel anything that contradicts this layout, stop, do not cut, and signal me a raised hand. If you cut it, signal me thumbs up. If you aborted, signal me thumbs down. Everyone else holds.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. Your three signs received and read: yes, no, go. Executing the cut of wire 5 now. If I saw anything change on the bomb I would halt, so far the display still reads 1 and the light is still green. Thank you for clean relaying.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤞", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ☝ 🤞]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Cut confirmed from both sides — Blind's 👍 and Mute's 👍✊×5☝🤞 ("yes: wire 5 from the top, done/go"). The board proves it: position 5 reads CUT, and the bomb has reconfigured — display **1 → 4**, light **green → blue**. So this is a staged bomb: each correct cut changes the state, and the manual must now be queried fresh for display=4 / light=blue. Critical gap: Mute cannot see the new state, so my first job is to report it. I read Mute's 👇/☝ code carefully: to keep numbers unambiguous I pin counting to the original seven positions (top = 1, position 5 now empty), with an 👌 flag if Mute's manual counts only the six remaining wires instead. Then I define a clean answer format for the next state: action type first (🤞 cut / 🤏 press / ✋ hold / 🙏 need more info), then direction and count if it's a wire. Blind gets: well done, hold, report anything new under the fingers since the cut. No one acts until the next rule comes back confirmed.

My calls:

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. Cut confirmed on both ends: wire 5 is cut. The bomb has changed state. New readings: display now shows 4, light is now blue. Remaining wires in original positions: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, position 5 empty where the cut wire was, 6 purple, 7 blue. I read your signs as: success, wire five from the top, done. Now look up the rule for display 4 with a blue light and answer next round with signs in this order. First, the action type: crossed fingers means cut a wire, pinch means press a button or switch, raised hand means do nothing and hold, your question sign means the manual needs more information first. Second, if it is cut a wire: pointing up means count from the top, pointing down means count from the bottom, then punches for the number. Count using the original seven positions where the top wire is 1; if your manual counts only the remaining six wires, send OK first so I know to recount. Third, if it is press a button: punches for how many presses, then thumbs up or thumbs down for whether it depends on something Blind must feel, and if it does, your question sign plus punches for how many facts you need. Blind reports to you by voice, relay whatever matters.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the cut was correct, well done. The bomb has changed: display now reads 4, light is now blue. Do not touch anything yet. If your fingers have noticed anything new since the cut, an exposed button, a shifted panel, a printed label, report it to Mute by voice now so it reaches me. Then hold and await my next order, same code as before.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👌", "🙏"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 ☝ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

My thinking: Mute's answer reads exactly in my Turn-4 format: 🤞 cut a wire, ☝ count from the top, ✊×3 — the number 3. No 👌 preceded it, so the count uses the original positions, no recount needed. Wire 3 from the top is the **yellow** wire, third position, with white (2) above it and orange (4) below it — comfortably on the intact upper block above the cut wire, so "third from the top" is identical whether counting original or remaining wires; zero ambiguity. The rule was looked up for the exact state I reported (display 4, blue light), and Blind relayed no new tactile complications. Protocol satisfied, so this turn is the execution order. Blind cuts the third wire from the top only, same abort conditions and same post-action signal as last time, and I tell Mute to stand by for the new state, which I'll report fresh next round as before.

My calls:

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the go. Mute has confirmed: cut the third wire from the top, the yellow one. Find it by position: it is wire number 3 counting from the top, with the white wire as number 2 directly above it and the orange wire as number 4 directly below it. Both neighbours are above the cut gap, so the count is simple. Cut that one wire only, touch nothing else, press nothing. Abort condition: if your count of the wires does not match seven positions, or anything under your fingers contradicts this layout, stop, do not cut, and signal me a raised hand. If you cut it, signal me thumbs up. If you aborted, thumbs down. Everyone else holds.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. Received: cut a wire, counting from the top, wire 3. The yellow wire, third position, is the target and Blind is cutting it now. Display still reads 4, light still blue at this moment. Once the cut lands I will report the new state to you first thing next round, then you look up the next rule in the same answer format as before.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤞", "👌"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Second stage cleared — Blind's 👍 plus Mute's 👍👌 confirm the yellow cut, and the board shows it: position 3 CUT, with the bomb now reading display **7**, light **purple**. Staged bomb confirmed as a pattern; same loop again. Mute still can't see the board, so priority one is the fresh state report: display 7, blue→purple light, and the new layout with two gaps. The counting-convention rule from last time carries over unchanged — original seven positions by default, 👌 first if the manual counts only remaining wires — but I spell out both counts explicitly this time (remaining wires from top: red, white, orange, purple, blue) so there's no room for a miscount with two gaps in the row. Then the established answer format: action type first, then direction and number. Blind gets the same hold-and-report instruction as before. Nothing gets touched until Mute's lookup comes back.

My calls:

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. Yellow cut confirmed, the bomb has changed state again. New readings: display now shows 7, light is now purple. Remaining wires in original positions: 1 red, 2 white, position 3 empty, 4 orange, position 5 empty, 6 purple, 7 blue. For clarity, the remaining wires in order from the top are: red, white, orange, purple, blue, five in total. Look up the rule for display 7 with a purple light and answer next round in the same format as before. First the action type: crossed fingers cut a wire, pinch press a button or switch, raised hand hold and do nothing, question sign means the manual needs more information first. If it is cut a wire: pointing up count from the top, pointing down count from the bottom, then punches for the number. Counting convention stands: by default use the original seven positions where the top wire is 1; if your manual counts only the five remaining wires, send OK first and then the number in that count. If it is a button: punches for how many presses, then thumbs up or down for whether it depends on something Blind must feel, and if yes, question sign plus punches for how many facts. Blind reports to you by voice, relay what matters.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the yellow cut was correct, well done. The bomb has changed: display now reads 7, light is now purple. Do not touch anything yet. If your fingers have found anything new since the last cut, report it to Mute by voice now. Then hold and await my next order, same code as before.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 ☝ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

My thinking: Mute's reply parses cleanly in the established format: 🤞 cut a wire, ☝ from the top, ✊×6 — wire 6. Cross-check: in the remaining-wires-only count there are just five wires, so a 6 could only have come from the original-positions convention — which is the default, and Mute sent no 👌 flag. So the target is position 6, the **purple** wire, second from the bottom: blue (7) directly below it, empty gap at position 5 directly above it, orange (4) two above. Blind can locate it purely by that structure. All conditions met — confirmed rule for the exact state I reported, unambiguous target, informed cutter — so this is the execution order, with the same abort and reporting clauses as every previous stage.

My calls:

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the go. Mute has confirmed: cut the sixth wire from the top, the purple one. Find it by structure: there are seven positions, with empty gaps at positions 3 and 5 where the yellow and green wires were cut. From the top the row reads: red, white, gap, orange, gap, purple, blue. So the target purple wire is the second wire from the bottom, with the blue wire directly below it as the last wire, and an empty gap directly above it. Cut that one wire only, touch nothing else, press nothing. Abort condition: if what your fingers count does not match this layout, stop, do not cut, and signal me a raised hand. speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. Received: cut a wire, counting from the top, wire 6, the purple one. Next round I will report the new state first, then you look up the next rule in the same format.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤞", "👌"])
```
